School Dinners
The price of school dinners is set by Portsmouth City Council and our caterers Caterlink. The cost of school dinners are £2.86 per day. All dinners must be paid for on the day or in advance via the online SCO pay system.
Children in Key Stage 1 already get free school meals – Universal Infant Free School Meals (UISFM). For children in Year 3 upwards you will need to apply for free school meals if you haven’t already. If you are not sure it’s worth applying as for every free school meal child the school gets an additional £1,320 to spend on the children themselves. Please see the front office for more details or you can apply online via Portsmouth City Council using this link: Free school meals – Portsmouth City Council
If you know your child is going to be late to school, please inform the office of their lunch choice before 9.15am otherwise you will need to provide a packed lunch.
If your child has any special dietary needs (e.g. No dairy, no soya) then please contact the office and we can arrange with Caterlink a menu catered to your child’s needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Learning Mentors - Portsdown Primary School & Early Years
pageCache.text:
Info
Learning Mentors
News
A message from your Learning Mentors
Portsdown Primary school currently employs two Learning Mentors; Mrs Blades and Mrs Jordan.
Our role is to ‘Remove the barriers to learning’ which prevent a child from reaching their full potential.
We support all our pupils, however, there are times when some of our pupils may find their friendships, confidence, emotions, feelings or behaviour overwhelming.
Through discussions with staff, parents and the pupil, we will develop a bespoke service to meet each child’s individual needs.
This support can be provided for a specific amount of time or on-going throughout a child’s time with us and can be delivered through 1:1 support, group work outside of the classroom as well as in-class support.
We believe in building strong honest relationships with our pupils and our parents.
We also run after school clubs that encourage confidence and self esteem which in turn helps to build friendships.
If you would like any more information, advice or simply a chat please feel free to come and talk to us.
Mrs Blades and Mrs Jordan.
Or contact us via our emails:
t.blades@portsdown.portsmouth.sch.uk
a.jordan@portsdown.portsmouth.sch.uk
OUR TRAINING
We have both completed the following training;
Accredited Learning Mentor training.
Foundation degree in Learning Support
Emotional First Aid,
Restorative Practices and
Mrs. Blades is trained in Loss Companions this enables her to help and support our children and family’s through their bereavement. Loss can come in many forms for example; death of a loved one, family pets, divorce, moving home and moving to a new school. Mrs. Blades is Youth Mental Health First Aid Champion for the school.
If you would like any more information please contact Mrs. Blades.
t.blades@portsdown.portsmouth.sch.uk
Some Wellbeing Tips from us to you
We all know how much better we feel after a good night’s sleep refreshed, happy and ready for the day ahead.
Sometimes, getting to sleep is not easy for both children and adults.
So we wondered if it might help to have a Portsdown bedtime routine
Mrs Jordan believes in a regular bedtime routine. She likes to go to bed at about the same time each night (except for News Year Eve when she likes to say
HAPPY NEW YEAR EVERBODY
A regular bedtime routine encourages a good sleep pattern.
So what is a good bedtime routine?
Starting to wind the day down at a set time each day:
Bath and story for younger children.
Bath and quiet chat with you about their day for older children before they settle in their bed for some alone time before lights out.
Mrs Blades enjoys relaxing before going to bed and she has a nice cuddle and chat with her dog Indie about her day.
Older children might wind down by reading a book, listening to music or practising breathing for relaxation.
Have a regular bedtime routine.
Mrs Blades loves to have a nap during the day but she finds it difficult at work!
Mrs Blades also knows that if she does sneak a nap (without Mr Vaghela noticing) she will find it hard to sleep that night.
Most children stop napping around 3-5 years of age. Some children over the age of 5 still like a nap but it is best to keep the nap to about 20 minutes and no later than early afternoon. As later naps can make it harder for children to sleep at night.
Mrs Jordan feels safe when she goes to bed because she sleeps with all her teddies. She also has her night light on to help her feel safe.
Sometimes, children feel scared about going to bed or being in the dark, praising your child and using a reward chart can help them feel brave.
Avoiding scary movies and computer games before bedtime.
Mrs Jordan finds it difficult to sleep if her computer screen is still on as it has a blue light. She also has nice thick curtains so the street light outside doesn’t keep her awake.
Blue light from the computer screen, television, phones and tablets suppress melatonin levels which delays sleepiness.
Here are a couple of our top tips for sleeping.
If your child uses a night-light, choose a dim, warm-coloured globe, rather than a bright, white, cool-coloured globe.
Sometimes, Mrs Blades lays in bed looking at her clock- this is not good because she is very ratty if she does not get enough sleep
Top tip: If your child is checking the time often, encourage your child to move the clock or watch to a spot where they can’t see it from their bed.
Mrs Blades and Mrs Jordan love being outside as much as possible during the day. They know that regular exercise is a great way of having fun and helping them sleep at night.
Top tip: Encourage your child to get as much natural light as possible during the day, especially in the morning. Bright light suppresses melatonin. This helps your child feel awake and alert during the day and sleepy towards bedtime.
Mrs Blades and Mrs Jordan know that caffeine is in lots of different drinks- coffee, tea, and cola.
Try to avoid allowing your child to drink any of these drinks late afternoon and evening.
1) Mrs Jordan enjoys phoning her friend to have a chat to help her calm down.
2) Mrs Blades likes to go for walks with her dog Indie to help her calm down.
3) The Worry Tree, we love this resource and use this a lot.
4) Star breathing, you will often see us taking deep breaths in and out to help calm us down.
5) We go outside and blow bubbles or we pretend to blow bubbles- this helps us to concentrate on our breathing and calm down.
Another good tip is to think of a happy place or draw your happy place. When you do this it is a good idea to use you’re 5 Senses
What can I SEE- clouds, trees, colours, flowers, my toys
What can I HEAR- wind, rain, birds, traffic, voices, music
What can I SMELL- flowers, food, perfume.
What can I TOUCH- wall, sofa, chair, bed, toys.
What can I TASTE- my favourite food

Curriculum
News
Portsdown Primary School and Early Years Curriculum
Our Curriculum Intent
Year 5 had a great day exploring life as a Viking (although I do not think many of them wil be rushing out to buy pea soup in the near future!).
At Portsdown Primary School and Early Years, we follow the National Curriculum (for Years 1 -6) and the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory framework (for Nursery and Year R). These act as an introduction to the essential knowledge and skills that the children of Portsdown need to be educated citizens. It introduces them to the best that has been thought and said, and helps engender an appreciation of human creativity and achievement. Our curriculum is carefully sequenced so that all children can build on their knowledge, skills and develop their vocabulary throughout their time at Portsdown.
Portsdown’s Teaching And Learning Guidance
As a school, we aim to widen and enrich their life experiences beyond their starting points by providing a range of trips, visits and experiences throughout their time at Portsdown. We believe that being able to read with confidence and developing a love of reading is vital to our children if they are to succeed in the future. This is why reading is at the heart of our curriculum.
To find out more about upcoming trips, visits and experiences (and ones we have completed) go to our Facebook pages (see the home Page for links) and look here:

News
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE)
The school’s RSE policy can be found by following this link
PSHE & RSE Curriculum at Portsdown Primary School and Early Years
At Portsdown Primary School and Early Years, we believe that PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education) and RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) provide a vital foundation for our pupils’ personal development, wellbeing and safety.
We aim to equip pupils with the knowledge, skills and values they need to lead safe, healthy and fulfilling lives. Through a carefully planned and sequenced curriculum, pupils develop a positive sense of self, respect for others, and the confidence to make informed decisions.
We use the Kapow Primary RSE & PSHE scheme from Year R to Year 6 (supplemented by Project Evolve for online safety). This scheme meets all the requirements of the statutory Relationships, Sex and Health Education (2025) set out by the Department for Education.
Our RSE curriculum is carefully sequenced and progressive, ensuring that knowledge and skills build appropriately across year groups in line with pupils’ age and developmental stage.
Key curriculum themes include:
Online Safety and Digital Literacy (via Kapow and/or Project Evolve)
Pupils are explicitly taught about:
Consent, Boundaries and Personal Safety
Pupils are taught, in an age-appropriate way:
Puberty and Human Reproduction
Our curriculum topics on puberty and human reproduction are structured as follows:
How We Teach PSHE & RSE
At Portsdown, we teach weekly personal, social, health and economic (PSHE) education lessons in order to teach the knowledge and skills in a developmental and age-appropriate way. PSHE lessons are reinforced through assemblies, wider curriculum opportunities, the school ethos, praise and reward systems, external visitors and Learning Mentors.
Information for Parents
Parents are able to access the Kapow Parent Portal for detailed information about what we are teaching and to which year group.
Access the Kapow Parent Portal
Parents and carers have the right to view RSE & PSHE teaching materials – we encourage you to contact your child’s class teacher if you would like to see resources in more detail.
Parents do not have the right to withdraw their children from relationships education.
Parents have the right to withdraw their children from the non-statutory components of sex education within RSE.
Requests for withdrawal should be put in writing using the form found in Appendix 1 of the RSE policy (available via the link on this page) and addressed to the headteacher.
For full details about our approach to RSE, please read our complete RSE policy (which is available by the aforementioned link on this page).
Frequently Asked Questions
When will my child learn about puberty? Learning about puberty begins in Year 3 and continues progressively through to Year 6, with content carefully matched to pupils’ age and development.
What if I have questions about what my child is learning? Please contact your child’s class teacher or our PSHE/RSE Subject Coordinator . We’re happy to discuss the curriculum and show you the resources we use.
How does the school ensure teaching is age-appropriate? We follow the Kapow scheme which is carefully sequenced to ensure content is developmentally appropriate. All teaching is delivered by trained staff in a safe, supportive environment.
If you have any questions about PSHE or RSE at Portsdown Primary School, please contact:
Deputy Headteacher: Darran Cowell Email: d.cowell@portsdown.portsmouth.sch.uk

Info
Meet The Governors
News
Want to Help Our School?
Become a Governor!
Stepping into the role of a school governor is one of the most impactful ways to give back to your community. It’s less about “running the school” (leave the daily bells and whistles to the Headteacher) and more about providing strategic leadership and accountability.
Think of it as being on a board of directors for a non-profit where the “profit” is a child’s future.
Each individual governor is a member of a governing body and all decisions are the joint responsibility of the governing body. There are different types of governors.
Associate members and advisors
The full Governing Body meet at least six times a year.
Governors have to act in accordance with the legislation and guidance from the Department of Education.
Parents may contact the Governors directly, but for general school matters, it is usually more appropriate to see the Class Teacher or Headteacher first.
Governors’ Minutes The minutes of governor meetings are public documents and are open to be viewed by any interested person.
Minutes are available to be read, at school, where the Headteacher, Deputy Headteacher or a member of the Governing Body could be available to answer any questions and explain the context of the issues raised in the minutes. This is to ensure that minutes read in isolation are not misinterpreted.

Our School Day
News
The school days starts at 8:45am and finishes at 3:15pm
The classroom will be open for registration at 8:45am and close at 9:00am
If you know your child is going to be late to school, please inform the office of their lunch choice before 9.30am otherwise you will need to provide a packed lunch.
Reception playtime starts at 10:15am
Playtime for the rest of the school is from 10:30am to 10:45am
Reception and Year 1 lunchtime is 11:45am – 12:30pm
Years 2 & 3 lunchtime is 12:00pm – 12:45pm
Years 4, 5 & 6 lunchtime is 12:25pm – 1:10pm
At the beginning and the end of the school day parents are asked to drop off and collect their children at the classroom doors. If normal arrangements need to be changed, e.g you are running late or another person is collecting your child, please let the teacher or the office know. This avoids any confusion or upset, especially for the younger children.
If you need a longer conversation with the teacher please make an appointment with them or via the front office. They are more than happy to meet parents.

Uniform
News
At Portsdown, we are very aware of the pressures of cost when it comes to school uniform. As a result, we have developed our approach to support all of our community. Any branded item is entirely optional.
If you do not want to buy branded items of uniform, non-branded items are readily available at leading supermarkets at a reasonable cost. The uniform with our school logo is sold through ‘My Clothing’.
The prices for branded items are very competitive and there is quite an extensive range to choose from. Please use the link below. https://myclothing.com/portsdown-primary-school/15288.school
Our uniform for the school is:
Black shoes or trainers (no backless or open toed shoes or shoes with a heel no higher than 1 inch)
Red cardigan, red sweatshirt, red jumper or red fleece – with or without school logo
White Polo Shirts (with or without school logo) or plain white shirts or blouses
Black or Grey trousers, skirt or pinafore – plain no embellishment
Black or grey shorts or a red gingham dress for the summer months – plain no embellishment
No jewellery with the exception of stud earrings or items of a religious or cultural nature. We may ask for these items to be removed during certain PE sessions.
PE KIT
Plain white t-shirt
Plain black or blue shorts
Primsole or trainers
In cold weather, children will be able to wear a jumper or plain track suit bottoms for outdoor PE. Book bags
When your child first starts at Portsdown we will give you registration forms to fill out. When you have filled out all of the forms, including the electronic free school meal form, we will give you a free Portsdown book bag.
If you prefer, you can purchase a book bag directly from the school office for £8.
School Uniform Policy is available on the main policies page.

pageCache.pageTitle: Remote Learning - Portsdown Primary School & Early Years
pageCache.text:
Info
Remote Learning
Remote Learning
News
Government guidance for Remote learning can be found here and the school’s approach is guided by this guidance. Providing remote education: guidance for schools – GOV.UK (www.gov.uk)
Portsdown Primary School & Early Years – Remote Learning
Overview
At Portsdown Primary School, we aim for all pupils to attend school in person. Remote learning is only provided when a child cannot attend school safely or due to health reasons, or in line with government guidance. It is not a substitute for attending school.
Remote learning ensures your child can continue to learn and stay connected to school while they are temporarily unable to be in the classroom.
When Remote Learning May Be Used
Remote learning is considered when:
School is closed for health, safety, or government guidance reasons.
Individual pupils cannot attend due to:
Illness or recovery from surgery/injury
Special educational needs or disabilities (SEND)
Mental health challenges
Important: Remote learning is not used for disciplinary reasons.
What Remote Learning Looks Like
KS1: 3 hours per day
KS2: 4 hours per day
Core subjects: English, Maths, and Reading every day
Other subjects: Covered if remote learning lasts 3+ consecutive days
Online resources through Google Classroom (teacher videos, Oak National Academy, BBC Bitesize)
Paper work packs for families without reliable internet access
Work is differentiated to meet your child’s learning needs.
Supporting Your Child
Staff provide guidance and explanations in daily tasks.
Learning is structured to help your child:
Understand instructions
Reflect and review their learning
Teachers and teaching assistants provide praise and acknowledgment of work
Weekly celebrations may include virtual assemblies, certificates, or stickers
Communication with Parents
Teachers will contact parents and children at least once a week via phone or email to support learning.
If you have concerns or questions, contact the school via the year group email or phone.
Respectful communication helps us provide the best support.
Safeguarding and Online Safety
All remote learning follows strict safeguarding and online safety guidelines.
Children should only use school-approved devices for learning.
Login details should not be shared.
Any online lessons (e.g., Zoom) are supervised, conducted safely, and follow professional standards for staff.
Parental Support
Parents can help by:
Checking that your child completes daily learning tasks.
Ensuring your child has a safe, quiet space to learn.
Contacting the school if your child has difficulties accessing resources or completing work.
Links to Policies (see the policies section of the wbsite for further details)
Remote learning follows and supports:
Behaviour & Relationships Policy
Child Protection & Safeguarding Policy
Data Protection & E-Safety Policy
Summary
Remote learning at Portsdown Primary ensures:
Children continue learning when they cannot attend school
Structured and differentiated lessons are provided
Engagement, feedback, and safeguarding are maintained
Parents are supported to help children succeed at home
This is a summary of our approach. For further details, please see the school’s Remote Learning Policy.To request a free paper copy of the Remote Learning Policy, please contact the school office by phone, email or pop into the offce and speak to a member of staff.
